parts.name: carp
sources: World: a smooth skin around the bones of World (World.Blob), fins and eyes (scripts/fish_template.exs). AGPL-3.0, as World
A common carp (cá chép, Cyprinus carpio): about 50 cm long, a robust body, a long dorsal fin, a forked tail fin, a dark gold coat with a darker back and a pale belly, bronze fins.

Wikipedia, Common carp (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_carp): "The average size of the common carp is around 40–80 cm (16–31 inches) and 2–14 kg"; wild carp are "typically slimmer than domesticated forms, with body length about four times body height"; "a tapering dorsal fin running down the last two-thirds of its body"; "a dark gold sheen that is most prominent on its head"; the caudal and anal fins "a dark bronze or washed with a rubbery orange hue".

The body of the template is the body of a domesticated carp (the length of the body about three times its depth); the carp of a pond is a little slimmer (body_depth 0.9). The time and the length of a wave of the swim: a guess. The shape and the colors next to photos of iNaturalist: https://www.inaturalist.org/photos/443517060, https://www.inaturalist.org/photos/75060478.
No barbels: the template has no bones or plates for them.
